{"passages":[{"reference":"20.21","text":"But Peter ......... diōtata, God orders our affairs. For we have Annoubion with us, ..........ogon. For when we are staying in Antioch, from then on he will discuss nativity with us more candidly, as a friend.

And indeed, when the father set out by night for nearby Antioch with those whom Peter had instructed, together with Annoubion, at dawn the next day, before Peter came forward for the discussion, Appion and Athenodorus returned to Laodicea, having sent Simon on ahead, and began looking for the father. When Peter learned this, he ordered them to come in. After they had entered and sat down, they asked, “Where is Faustus?” Peter answered, “We do not know. For after coming to you that very evening, he was no longer seen by his own people. Yesterday at dawn Simon also looked for him, and since we gave him no answer, I do not know what came over him: he declared himself to be Faustus but was not believed, and, weeping and beating himself, he threatened to kill himself and rushed off as though toward the sea.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὁ θεὸς τὰ πράγματα ἡμῶν οἰκονομεῖ","chosen":"God orders our affairs","rationale":"οἰκονομεῖ denotes managing or arranging affairs; “orders” preserves the providential-management image without adding a theological explanation."},{"source_quote":"περὶ γενέσεως","chosen":"about nativity","rationale":"In the context of Annoubion and the preceding astrological controversy, γένεσις concerns birth or nativity in its astrological sense; “origin” remains lexically possible outside that context."},{"source_quote":"ὡς φίλος γνησιώτερον","chosen":"more candidly, as a friend","rationale":"γνησιώτερον can mean more genuinely, sincerely, or candidly; the comparison concerns the openness expected from a friend."},{"source_quote":"καὶ κοπτόμενος","chosen":"and beating himself","rationale":"κόπτομαι can describe striking oneself as a gesture of grief or mourning; the physical image is retained."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἐπὶ θάλασσαν ὥρμησε","chosen":"rushed off as though toward the sea","rationale":"ὡς makes the reported destination less direct than a simple statement that he reached or entered the sea."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ......... διώτατα ὁ θεὸς τὰ πράγματα ἡμῶν οἰκονομεῖ","issue":"The nine-dot printed lacuna removes wording after “Peter.” Its unavailable content has not been restored, and the exact nine dots are retained in the English.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"διώτατα","issue":"The image-checked print reads διώτατα, but that form has no defensible contextual analysis here as printed. It is transliterated rather than silently corrected; the adjacent lacuna prevents secure reconstruction.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"Ἀννουβίων .......... όγον","issue":"The ten-dot printed lacuna removes part or all of a description of Annoubion, leaving only the fragment όγον. The dots and the transliterated surviving fragment “ogon” are retained, and no restoration has been supplied.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.22","text":"On hearing this, Appion and those with him wailed and beat themselves, saying, “Why did you not receive him?” And just as Athenodorus was about to say to me, “It was Faustus, your father,” Appion forestalled him and said, “We learned from someone that Simon found him and sent him away ............................... the truth, Faustus himself having entreated him, because he did not wish to see his sons having become Jews. When we heard this, we came for this reason, looking for him. But since he is not here, the man who told us appears to have spoken truthfully. So we have told you just what we heard from him.”

But I, Clement, understood Peter’s purpose: he wanted to plant in them the suspicion that he intended to demand the old man from them, so that they would become afraid and flee. I therefore joined in furthering his plan and said to Appion, “Listen, my dearest Appion. We were eager to give him, as our father, what seemed good to us. But if he himself did not wish to receive it and, on the contrary, was disgusted with us and fled—to put it rather harshly—we do not care about him either.” When I said this, they left, offended as though at cruelty, and—as we learned the next day—....... us, they set out in Simon’s tracks for Judea.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐπολολύξαντες ἐκόψαντο","chosen":"wailed and beat themselves","rationale":"The two verbs respectively portray a loud lament and bodily striking as mourning; neither image is collapsed into generic grief."},{"source_quote":"ὁ Σίμων ἐξώρμησε","chosen":"Simon ... sent him away","rationale":"ἐξορμάω can be intransitive, “set out,” or causative, “send or drive out.” The preceding αὐτόν supports the causative rendering, but the following lacuna prevents certainty."},{"source_quote":"ὑπόνοιαν αὐτοῖς ἐνσπεῖραι","chosen":"to plant in them the suspicion","rationale":"The agricultural image of sowing or planting suspicion is preserved."},{"source_quote":"τὸν γέροντα ζητεῖν μέλλων παρ’ αὐτοῖς","chosen":"he intended to demand the old man from them","rationale":"ζητεῖν παρά may mean seek information or an accounting from them, or demand the man from them. “Demand” best explains why they would become afraid and flee, while the precise force remains uncertain."},{"source_quote":"βδελυξάμενος ἡμᾶς","chosen":"was disgusted with us","rationale":"βδελύσσομαι expresses abhorrence or revulsion, stronger than merely disliking or rejecting someone."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἐπ’ ὠμότητι δυσχεράναντες","chosen":"offended as though at cruelty","rationale":"ὡς marks their construal of Clement’s words as cruel rather than an unqualified narrator’s judgment that they were cruel."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὁ Σίμων ἐξώρμησε ............................... τὰ ἀληθῆ","issue":"The thirty-one-dot printed lacuna removes the construction connecting ἐξώρμησε with τὰ ἀληθῆ. The exact dots are retained, and no missing action or speech has been invented.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ (ὡς ἐμάθομεν τῆς ἄλλης) ἡμῶν ....... κατ’ ἴχνη Σίμωνος ἐπὶ τὴν Ἰουδαίαν ὥρμησαν","issue":"The seven-dot printed lacuna removes the wording governing or completing ἡμῶν. The supplied punctuation is also syntactically abrupt. The English preserves the gap and does not conjecturally complete the relation to “us.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.23","text":"Nevertheless, when ten days had passed, ......... from Antioch, from the father, reporting to us how the father, dēmo........., by denouncing his appearance and blessing Peter, had filled the entire city of the Antiochenes with longing. He further reported that consequently everyone desired to see him; that some, angry with him as though he were Simon because of his surpassing affection for Peter, even wanted to lay hands on Faustus as though he were Simon; and that therefore, fearing he might be killed, he had sent to ask Peter to come immediately, so that Peter might reach him while he was still alive and make a timely appearance before the city while its longing for him was at its height.

When Peter heard this, he gathered a great many people for assembly, appointed one of his followers as bishop, baptized and healed, and, after remaining three days in Laodicea, hastened to set out for nearby Antioch.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὴν πᾶσαν Ἀντιοχέων πόλιν εἰς πόθον μετέθηκεν","chosen":"had filled the entire city of the Antiochenes with longing","rationale":"The Greek literally describes moving the city into longing. The object of that longing is not expressed in this clause, so it is not added here."},{"source_quote":"αὐτοῦ μορφῆς κατηγορῶν","chosen":"denouncing his appearance","rationale":"αὐτοῦ may refer to the father’s present appearance, Simon’s appearance, or the person represented by it. The non-reflexive “his” preserves that referential ambiguity."},{"source_quote":"χαλεπαίνοντας αὐτῷ ὡς Σίμωνι","chosen":"angry with him as though he were Simon","rationale":"The contextual referent is Faustus under Simon’s appearance, but the pronoun itself does not explicitly name him."},{"source_quote":"διὰ τὴν πρὸς Πέτρον ὑπερβάλλουσαν στοργήν","chosen":"because of his surpassing affection for Peter","rationale":"στοργή denotes strong affection, and ὑπερβάλλουσαν supplies the exceptional or surpassing degree."},{"source_quote":"ὅπως αὐτὸν ζῶντα ἐπικαταλάβῃ","chosen":"so that Peter might reach him while he was still alive","rationale":"ἐπικαταλαμβάνω here means catch up with or reach someone; ζῶντα applies to the endangered Faustus."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὸ ἐκκλησιάζειν πλείστους συναγαγών","chosen":"he gathered a great many people for assembly","rationale":"ἐκκλησιάζειν can mean convening or addressing an assembly and need not by itself denote a later formal church service."},{"source_quote":"ἐπίσκοπον ἐκ τῶν ἀκολούθων καταστήσας","chosen":"appointed one of his followers as bishop","rationale":"ἐπίσκοπος denotes the appointed overseer; “bishop” preserves the office term used by the narrative."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"πλὴν ἡμερῶν δέκα διελθουσῶν ......... ἐκ τῆς Ἀντιοχείας παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἀγγελῶν ἡμῖν","issue":"The nine-dot printed lacuna removes the main subject and/or verbal wording before the masculine participle ἀγγελῶν. The resulting fragment is retained without inventing a messenger or finite verb.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὁ πατὴρ δημο......... αὐτοῦ μορφῆς κατηγορῶν","issue":"The nine-dot printed lacuna follows the surviving fragment δημο and removes the remainder of the word or phrase. The English retains that fragment as “dēmo” followed by exactly nine dots; no adverb such as “publicly” has been restored.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
